title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #7

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Singular means (1 mark)
   A. one
   B. none
   C. many
   D. half

2. Plural means (1 mark)
   A. more than one
   B. nothing
   C. only one
   D. the biggest

3. In a singing game, who gives the instructions? (1 mark)
   A. The audience only
   B. The oldest pupil always
   C. Nobody
   D. The soloist

4. Why should you underline new words in a text? (1 mark)
   A. To spoil the book
   B. So you can find their meanings and learn them
   C. To hide them
   D. To count pages

5. Reading a text once for the general meaning is done (1 mark)
   A. first, before looking at details
   B. last, after everything
   C. only with a partner
   D. never

6. What does legible writing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing very small
   B. Writing that can be read easily
   C. Writing in capital letters only
   D. Writing with a red pen

7. Which pencil grip is best? (1 mark)
   A. Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   B. Hold it by the end with your teeth
   C. Grip it with a fist
   D. Press it very hard

8. Tall letters such as b and d usually reach (1 mark)
   A. the bottom of the page
   B. the top line
   C. below the base line
   D. the edge of the desk

9. What should listeners do after a group reads aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at the readers
   B. Give kind and helpful feedback
   C. Leave the room
   D. Tear the script

10. How can recording your reading help you? (1 mark)
   A. It deletes the story
   B. It ends practice
   C. You can listen back and see how to improve
   D. It makes you forget

11. Which word must begin with a capital letter in the middle of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. weather
   B. Monday
   C. cloud
   D. morning

12. In grammar, a verb is a word that (1 mark)
   A. names a place
   B. shows an action
   C. joins two sentences
   D. names a person

13. Which sentence belongs to the main idea Fire is dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. Never play with matches.
   B. The market is far.
   C. Maize is tasty.
   D. Rain is wet.

14. What is a tongue twister? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of drum
   B. A very long word
   C. A phrase that is hard to say fast
   D. A silent poem

15. What is a good rule for handling library books? (1 mark)
   A. Write in them
   B. Turn pages gently and return them on time
   C. Fold the corners
   D. Leave them outside

16. What does the English proverb Look before you leap teach? (1 mark)
   A. Never move
   B. Think before you act
   C. Jump quickly
   D. Look at the floor

17. Which is a character in a story? (1 mark)
   A. The end
   B. A girl called Neema
   C. A shady tree
   D. The rainy season

18. Which sentence uses when correctly? (1 mark)
   A. When we ran home rained it.
   B. Rained we when home.
   C. We when ran.
   D. When it rained, we ran home.

19. Which value should be shown in a market skit? (1 mark)
   A. Honesty, such as giving correct change
   B. Rudeness
   C. Stealing
   D. Cheating

20. How should you speak when narrating an event? (1 mark)
   A. Without stopping
   B. Angrily always
   C. Very quietly
   D. Clearly and with feeling

21. Where can the main idea often be found? (1 mark)
   A. In the page number
   B. Nowhere
   C. In the first sentence of a paragraph
   D. Only in the last word

22. What does change mean in a shop? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. The clothes
   C. Money given back after paying
   D. A journey

23. What is a mosaic? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of song
   B. A picture made of small pieces
   C. A long story
   D. A heavy load

24. What does it mean to advocate for animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. To ignore them
   B. To speak in support of caring for animals
   C. To harm animals
   D. To hide them

25. What is a refrain? (1 mark)
   A. A rhyme only
   B. The title
   C. A line that is repeated
   D. A page

26. What should you check in a partner's story? (1 mark)
   A. Only the pen
   B. Only the paper colour
   C. Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   D. Nothing

27. What does a picture story use? (1 mark)
   A. Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   B. Only numbers
   C. Only names
   D. Only maps

28. Which tense is used to tell a story about what happened? (1 mark)
   A. Only questions
   B. Only the future
   C. No tense
   D. The past tense

29. How should you start a new speaker's words in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. On a new line
   B. Inside a bracket
   C. On the same line as before
   D. At the end of the page

30. What is role play? (1 mark)
   A. Acting out a situation
   B. Copying
   C. Reading silently
   D. Drawing only

31. Which is the first step in writing a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Write the ending only
   B. Draw the border
   C. Choose the theme and characters
   D. Sign it

32. Which is a polite phrase to ask someone to repeat? (1 mark)
   A. Could you repeat that, please?
   B. Stop talking
   C. What did you say?
   D. Say it again now

33. What is a quote in news? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. A map
   C. A price
   D. The exact words of a person

34. Which is a difference between an advert and a news item? (1 mark)
   A. News is always a poem
   B. Adverts report elections only
   C. They are exactly the same
   D. An advert tries to sell and news reports facts

35. What is an advertisement? (1 mark)
   A. A poem
   B. A lesson
   C. A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   D. A weather report

36. What is a digital form? (1 mark)
   A. A paper airplane
   B. A form made of clay
   C. A form on a tree
   D. A form filled in on a device

37. Which is a rude phrase? (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Pardon me
   C. Shut up
   D. Please continue

38. Why do we read poems? (1 mark)
   A. To stop reading
   B. To waste time
   C. To hide feelings
   D. To enjoy language and learn lessons

39. What is a line in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. One row of words
   B. A stanza
   C. A book
   D. A whole page

40. In writing, what is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A poem
   B. A story
   C. A picture
   D. Words telling someone what to do

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. List the verbs in: Otieno touched the handle and the water splashed. (3 marks)

42. Give three parts of a news item. (3 marks)

43. List three steps for skimming. (3 marks)

44. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

45. Describe how to read a passage with interjections aloud. (4 marks)

46. Describe how a group can read a text aloud together and give feedback. (4 marks)

47. Write a four-sentence paragraph on washing hands. Use first, next, then and finally. (4 marks)

48. List three habits of an attentive listener. (3 marks)

49. Describe how you would scan a passage to find how much a box of mangoes costs. (4 marks)

50. List three ways of taking good care of a domestic animal. (3 marks)

51. Plan a story that uses the proverb Many hands make light work. Give the title, characters, problem and ending. (4 marks)

52. What is a vocabulary bank and why is it useful? (2 marks)

53. Describe how you would play Simon says with your class and say what it teaches. (5 marks)

54. Write a short story of five sentences that ends with the proverb A stitch in time saves nine. (5 marks)

55. Give three money words and their meanings. (3 marks)

56. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

57. Add capital letters, commas and full stops: on friday we bought rice beans and flour (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #7 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — one
   A singular noun names one person, animal, place or thing.

2. A — more than one
   Plural nouns name two or more.

3. D — The soloist
   The soloist leads by singing the instructions and the group responds.

4. B — So you can find their meanings and learn them
   Underlining marks the words to study.

5. A — first, before looking at details
   A first reading gives the main idea.

6. B — Writing that can be read easily
   Legible means easy to read.

7. A — Hold it lightly between the thumb and first finger
   A light grip prevents tiredness.

8. B — the top line
   Tall letters go up to the top line.

9. B — Give kind and helpful feedback
   Feedback helps readers improve.

10. C — You can listen back and see how to improve
   Playing back shows where to improve.

11. B — Monday
   Days of the week begin with capital letters.

12. B — shows an action
   Verbs show actions.

13. A — Never play with matches.
   It is a detail about fire safety.

14. C — A phrase that is hard to say fast
   Tongue twisters train clear speech.

15. B — Turn pages gently and return them on time
   Good care keeps books usable for others.

16. B — Think before you act
   It advises careful thought before doing something.

17. B — A girl called Neema
   Characters are the people or animals.

18. D — When it rained, we ran home.
   It shows two events joined by time.

19. A — Honesty, such as giving correct change
   Skits can show good values.

20. D — Clearly and with feeling
   Clear speech and feeling make a story good.

21. C — In the first sentence of a paragraph
   First sentences often give the main idea.

22. C — Money given back after paying
   Change is the money you get back.

23. B — A picture made of small pieces
   A mosaic is made of small pieces of paper or seeds.

24. B — To speak in support of caring for animals
   Advocating means speaking in support.

25. C — A line that is repeated
   A refrain is repeated in a poem or song.

26. C — Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   Peer review checks the elements.

27. A — Pictures showing the beginning, middle and end
   A picture story tells events with drawings.

28. D — The past tense
   Stories about past events use the past.

29. A — On a new line
   A new line shows a new speaker.

30. A — Acting out a situation
   Role play acts a scene.

31. C — Choose the theme and characters
   Planning comes first.

32. A — Could you repeat that, please?
   Please and could show politeness.

33. D — The exact words of a person
   A quote repeats what someone said.

34. D — An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   Their purposes differ.

35. C — A message that tells about a product or service to attract buyers
   Adverts promote products or services.

36. D — A form filled in on a device
   Digital forms are filled on phones or computers.

37. C — Shut up
   Shut up is disrespectful.

38. D — To enjoy language and learn lessons
   Poems entertain and teach.

39. A — One row of words
   Poems are written in lines.

40. D — Words telling someone what to do
   Instructions say what to do.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: touched, splashed
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb and one mark for ignoring the nouns.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Headline, lead, details, quote (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read headings, read the first sentence of each paragraph, glance over the rest, say the main idea.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, find the interjections, decide the feeling of each, read each with the right voice, and keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, help each other with hard words, take turns to read, then listen to the group and give one good point and one point to improve in a kind way.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct parts.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: First, wet your hands. Next, rub soap on them. Then rinse them. Finally, dry them with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct step in order and sequence word.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Face the speaker, stay quiet, think about the words, wait for your turn, respond correctly (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each habit, up to three.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Know that you are looking for the price, run your eyes over the text looking for numbers, stop at the number, read the sentence around it and check that it answers the question.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide a shelter, take it to a veterinary doctor when sick, do not overload it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any suitable plan, for example Title: The Clean Compound. Characters: pupils. Problem: a dirty compound. Ending: everyone helps and it is clean quickly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is a class list of words on one theme. It helps pupils remember and use new words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the use.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: One pupil is the leader. The leader gives instructions. Pupils obey only when the leader says Simon says. Those who obey a wrong instruction are out. The game teaches careful listening.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the leader, one for the rule, one for what happens when a player breaks the rule, and two marks for explaining what it teaches.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five clear sentences with a beginning, problem, ending and the proverb used correctly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence up to four and one mark for using the proverb correctly.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trade: buying and selling. Profit: money gained. Customer: person who buys. Price: cost of something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word with its meaning.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: On Friday we bought rice, beans and flour.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capitals, one mark for the commas, one for the full stop.
